title: Braided sheaf tensor and its sheafification generators
statement:
Fix a universe $\mathcal V$. Let $(C,J)$ be a $\mathcal V$-small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category relative to $\mathcal V$, with $\mathcal V$-small morphism sets [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]. Give $\mathcal A$ a monoidal structure [def-sfb-monoidal-category] which is closed (each $M\otimes-$ has a right adjoint) and braided (natural isomorphisms $M\otimes N\cong N\otimes M$ satisfying the two hexagon identities); symmetry is not assumed. Let $U:\operatorname{Sh}(C,J;\mathcal A)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$ be the full inclusion and $a\dashv U$ sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For presheaves put $(P\otimes_p Q)(V)=P(V)\otimes Q(V)$, with restriction maps the tensors of the restriction maps, and let $\underline{\mathbf1}$ be the constant presheaf at the tensor unit.

The sheafified pointwise tensor $F\otimes G=a(UF\otimes_p UG)$ and unit $\mathbf1_C=a(\underline{\mathbf1})$ carry the canonical braided monoidal structure, for which $a$ is strong braided monoidal. Write $t_{F,G}:UF\otimes_p UG\to U(F\otimes G)$ and $u:\underline{\mathbf1}\to U\mathbf1_C$ for the sheafification unit maps. They are natural transformations of presheaves, and $t_{F,G}$ is natural in both sheaves. For every sheaf $H$, precomposition with these maps gives bijections
$$
\operatorname{Hom}(F\otimes G,H)\ \cong\ \operatorname{Nat}(UF\otimes_p UG,UH),\qquad
\operatorname{Hom}(\mathbf1_C,H)\ \cong\ \operatorname{Nat}(\underline{\mathbf1},UH).
$$
In particular these precompositions detect equality of morphisms. The same assertions hold for a site essentially $\mathcal V$-small after passage to a small skeleton.

source.place: Proof, first sentence, with the closed braided hypotheses of the statement; general braided form of the sheafified pointwise tensor construction.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal P=\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$, $I=\underline{\mathbf1}$ and $\eta_P:P\to UaP$ for the unit of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. The pointwise tensor is a bifunctor: its identity and composition equations are those of the coefficient tensor at each $V$. Applying the coefficient associator, unitors and braiding at each $V$ gives natural presheaf isomorphisms. Each pentagon, triangle and hexagon is the corresponding coefficient equation at $V$, so these give a braided monoidal structure on $\mathcal P$ [def-sfb-monoidal-category].

source.place: First sentence; pointwise braided tensor and notation.

proof.text: Define $W$ by the Hom test in [lem-sfb-local-equivalences-braided-tensor]. The adjunction [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] identifies that test for $f:P\to Q$ with bijectivity of $\operatorname{Hom}(af,H)$ for every sheaf $H$. This is equivalent to $af$ being invertible: surjectivity for $H=aP$ produces $g:aQ\to aP$ with $g(af)=1$; injectivity for $H=aQ$ then gives $(af)g=1$. Also $\eta_P\in W$, since its Hom test is exactly unique extension into every sheaf. Since $U$ is a full inclusion, its counit $\epsilon_F:aUF\to F$ is invertible: the inverse is the unique extension of $1_{UF}$, and both composites are identities by that same uniqueness.

source.place: First sentence; sheafification units and local maps.

proof.text:
By [lem-coef-grothendieck-small-limits], $\mathcal A$ has all $\mathcal V$-small limits: its Hom universe and Grothendieck colimit universe are exactly $\mathcal V$. Thus [lem-sfb-local-equivalences-braided-tensor] applies with this small $C$ and gives left and right tensor stability of $W$, without symmetry. In particular $\eta_P\otimes_p\eta_Q=(1\otimes_p\eta_Q)(\eta_P\otimes_p1)$ lies in $W$. Consequently
$$\Delta_{P,Q}=a(\eta_P\otimes_p\eta_Q):a(P\otimes_pQ)\xrightarrow{\sim}a(UaP\otimes_pUaQ)$$
is a natural isomorphism, by step 2.

source.place: First sentence; closed braided tensor stability and the two-unit comparison.

proof.text: Sheafification is a localization at $W$. Indeed it inverts $W$ by step 2. If $T:\mathcal P\to\mathcal E$ inverts $W$, extend it by $\overline T=TU$; the maps $T\eta_P$ give a natural isomorphism $T\xrightarrow{\sim}\overline T a$. Conversely for $S:\operatorname{Sh}\to\mathcal E$, $S\epsilon$ identifies $(Sa)U$ with $S$. These two natural isomorphisms give inverse equivalences on functor categories: the same formulas on a natural transformation commute by naturality of $\eta$ and $\epsilon$, and the triangle identities make the composites identities. This proves the full localization property, including morphisms, from the adjunction [def-weil-pbc-sheafification].

source.place: First sentence; reflector as a localization, with the factorization written out.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-braided-monoidal-localization] to $L=a$, the pointwise braided category of step 1, and the class $W$ of steps 2--3. Step 4 verifies its localization hypothesis. Denote its tensor on sheaves by $\diamond$, with unit $aI$ and strong braided tensor comparison $\mu_{P,Q}:aP\diamond aQ\xrightarrow{\sim}a(P\otimes_pQ)$. The lemma supplies the coherent associator, unitors and braiding for this tensor, and its unit comparison for $a$ is the identity.

source.place: First sentence; abstract braided localization, before identifying the prescribed tensor.

proof.text:
Put $F*G=a(UF\otimes_pUG)$ and $(f*g)=a(Uf\otimes_pUg)$, exactly the bifunctor in the statement. There is a natural isomorphism
$$c_{F,G}:F*G\xrightarrow{\mu_{UF,UG}^{-1}}aUF\diamond aUG\xrightarrow{\epsilon_F\diamond\epsilon_G}F\diamond G.$$
Here is explicitly how to use the coherent structure from step 5 on this prescribed bifunctor. For every parenthesized tensor expression $B$, define $c_B:B_*\to B_\diamond$ recursively: at a variable and the unit take the identity, and at $(D,E)$ take $(c_D\diamond c_E)c_{D_*,E_*}$. Define its associator, unitors and braiding by $c_{B'}^{-1}s^\diamond c_B$, where $s^\diamond:B_\diamond\to B'_\diamond$ is the corresponding old constraint. Naturality of $c_{F,G}$ shows that tensoring a constraint in any larger expression gives this same conjugation formula. Hence along every path in a pentagon, triangle or hexagon, successive factors $c_Bc_B^{-1}$ cancel. The path is $c_{\mathrm{target}}^{-1}$ times the old path times $c_{\mathrm{source}}$; the old paths agree by step 5. Thus all required coherence equations hold. This defines the braided structure on exactly $*$ with unit $aI$, rather than identifying the localization's chosen tensor with it by equality.

source.place: First sentence; explicit natural tensor comparison and cancellation proof of coherence.

proof.text:
For the structure of step 6, the strong tensor map of $a$ is $\mu_{P,Q}c_{aP,aQ}$. It equals $\Delta_{P,Q}^{-1}$. To check this, naturality of $\mu$ gives
$$\Delta_{P,Q}\mu_{P,Q}=\mu_{UaP,UaQ}(a\eta_P\diamond a\eta_Q).$$
Substitute the formula for $c_{aP,aQ}$ and use $\epsilon_{aP}a\eta_P=1$ and $\epsilon_{aQ}a\eta_Q=1$, the two triangle identities. The resulting composite $\mu_{P,Q}c_{aP,aQ}\Delta_{P,Q}$ is the identity. The unit comparison remains the identity of $aI$. Conjugation by the same $c$ in the associativity, unit and braided functor equations reduces each to the equation for $\mu$ in step 5, so $a$ is strong braided for this tensor. In particular its braiding is the canonical $a(\beta^p_{UF,UG})$: naturality of $\mu$ and of $\epsilon$ identifies this map, after $c$, with the old braiding. We henceforth write $\otimes$ for $*$.

source.place: First sentence; canonical strong braided comparisons on the prescribed tensor.

proof.text:
By definition $t_{F,G}=\eta_{UF\otimes_pUG}$ and $u=\eta_I$. The unit $\eta$ is a natural transformation of presheaves, so each of these is a presheaf map. For sheaf maps $f:F\to F'$ and $g:G\to G'$, its naturality at $Uf\otimes_pUg$ reads
$$U(f\otimes g)t_{F,G}=t_{F',G'}(Uf\otimes_pUg),$$
which is the required simultaneous naturality. For a sheaf $H$, the unique-extension property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] applied to $P=UF\otimes_pUG$ gives the first displayed Hom bijection by $h\mapsto U(h)t_{F,G}$. Applied to $P=I$ it gives the second by $h\mapsto U(h)u$. These are bijections of whole Hom sets, so their injectivity detects equality; no claim about generating individual sections is used.

source.place: First sentence and the use of objectwise tensor maps; the two universal generator tests.

proof.text: For an essentially $\mathcal V$-small site choose a $\mathcal V$-small skeleton and equip it with the induced covering topology. The assertion in the statement is expressly made after this passage: apply steps 1--8 on that small site. All diagrams for limits and all presheaf Hom tests above are then indexed in $\mathcal V$. This avoids taking ends over the original possibly larger object type.
